sections.label: Weapons regulated under Arms Explosives Act
sections.summary: MHA regulates six weapons under the Arms and Explosives Act: sword, spear, spearhead, dagger, bayonet, and certain dangerous bows and arrows.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) currently regulates six weapons under the Arms and Explosives Act (AEA) – sword, spear, spearhead, dagger, bayonet, and certain dangerous bows and arrows.

sections.label: Guns Explosives Weapons Control Act
sections.summary: MHA introduced the GEWCA in January 2021, replacing the AEA when in force end 2021, expanding the regulated weapons list with greater controls.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: In January 2021, MHA introduced the Guns, Explosives and Weapons Control Act (GEWCA), which will replace the AEA when it comes into force in end 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Under the GEWCA, the list of regulated weapons will be expanded and subject to greater controls.

sections.label: Age verification and suspicious transactions
sections.summary: MHA is considering requiring e-commerce platforms and brick-and-mortar retailers to verify age and prevent clearly underaged access, and is considering age verification for suspicious transaction reporting.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: So, we have to find the right balance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: We are currently considering requiring the e-commerce platforms, for example, as well as the brick-and-mortar retailers, to take reasonable steps to verify, do some age verification checks and ensure that those especially who are clearly underaged, do not have access to these items.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: On the second question about reporting suspicious transactions, we all recognise that, first of all, already requiring age verification is something that we would consider doing and there are some practical challenges there.

sections.label: MHA SPF support for schools
sections.summary: MHA and SPF work with schools and MOE on SGSecure security protocols, and SPF will continue strengthening awareness, checks, and response protocols for weapons incidents in schools.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: On the third question about what MHA and SPF are doing in support of MOE and the schools, we have been working with the schools and MOE to implement, for example, the SGSecure movement; there is a form of security protocols.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: SPF will continue to work with the schools and MOE to strengthen the awareness, the checks on, as well as the response protocol for some of these weapons incidents and checks in the schools.
